scope_summary: Finish coat application (1-2 coats) for primed drywall ceilings in new construction. Applied over cured primer. Ceilings painted BEFORE walls — NO edge work required. Wall painter establishes ceiling line. Mirrors SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH adapted for overhead work.
relevant_findings: NC production sequence: Prime all → Paint ceilings → Paint walls. Ceiling painter works first.
NO edge work at ceiling-wall boundary — walls haven't been painted yet and WILL be painted after
Ceiling painter can roll slightly onto wall area (1-2 inches) — wall painter covers this and establishes clean line
Edge work responsibility belongs in WALL finish spec, not ceiling spec
Spray+backroll is production standard for ceiling finish in NC (18-inch roller per doctrine)
Overhead work is approximately 15-20% slower than equivalent wall work
Flat or matte sheen typical for ceilings (hides imperfections, reduces glare)
Higher sheens (eggshell, satin, semi-gloss) are significantly harder on ceilings due to gravity — lap marks and roller marks more visible
QT2-QT3: single coat flat; QT4: two coats (flat for color OR eggshell or satin); QT5: two coats semi-gloss or gloss
QT4+ requires light sand between coats per doctrine
Recessed lighting cans and ceiling electrical boxes require protection from overspray
Window/door masking required — overspray fallout and roller splatter falls onto openings below
Window/door masking may already be in place from prime phase — verify intact or apply if missing
No floor protection for finished flooring (subfloor only in NC pre-trim typical)
Subfloor vacuum cleanup required after painting

clarifications_from_field.rationale: Walls have NOT been painted yet and WILL be painted after ceilings. Wall painter establishes the final ceiling line. Ceiling painter can roll into wall area without concern for perfect line.
NC pre-trim typically has subfloor only — no finished flooring to protect. If finished flooring is installed (phased occupancy), floor protection applies.
Overspray fallout and roller splatter from ceiling work falls down onto windows/doors. Masking may already be in place from priming phase — verify intact. If not in place, must be applied.
This spec assumes ceilings already primed per SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_NC_PRIME.

prep_requirements.method: Walk and inspect primed ceiling with work light. Mark imperfections.
Spackle defects, sand smooth, spot prime repairs
Pole sander with 220 grit, light pass to degloss and smooth
prep_requirements.reason: Improves adhesion and provides smooth base for finish coat

prep_requirements.method: Pole sander with 220 grit between coat 1 and coat 2
prep_requirements.reason: Smooths nibs and imperfections before second coat

prep_requirements.method: Stuff recessed cans with paper, tape over face. Stuff ceiling electrical boxes.
prep_requirements.reason: Prevent paint entering cans and junction boxes
prep_requirements.skip_conditions: Roll-only method (reduced risk, but still recommended)

prep_requirements.method: Verify existing masking from prime phase is intact, or apply if missing
prep_requirements.reason: Overspray fallout and splatter falls onto openings below
prep_requirements.skip_conditions: Always required for spray; recommended for roll

advantages: Two coat coverage for color depth

when_to_use: QT4 with eggshell or satin sheen

limitations: Shows every imperfection — requires critical prep
Significant sheen application penalty on ceilings

ceiling_to_wall_edge.reason: Walls not yet painted. Wall painter will establish ceiling line when painting walls. Ceiling painter can roll 1-2 inches onto wall area.

trim_edge.reason: Pre-trim phase — no crown molding installed

common_failure_modes.cause: Dry edge during rolling, inconsistent technique, working too slowly overhead
common_failure_modes.prevention: Maintain wet edge, work in sections, consistent roller pressure
common_failure_modes.remediation: Additional coat may hide minor lap marks

common_failure_modes.cause: Roller nap too heavy, paint too thick, insufficient backroll
common_failure_modes.prevention: Use appropriate nap (3/8-1/2"), proper thinning if needed, thorough backroll

common_failure_modes.cause: Inconsistent coverage, spot repairs showing through
common_failure_modes.prevention: Uniform application, proper coverage rate, touch up wet-on-wet

common_failure_modes.cause: Insufficient coverage, paint spread too thin
common_failure_modes.prevention: Proper coverage rate, don't over-spread paint

required_paintscope_keys.description: Floor area for subfloor vacuum cleanup
Room count for ceiling fixture protection heuristic
Count of window openings to mask (or verify masking)
Count of door openings to mask (or verify masking)

zones_identified.rationale: Recessed lights and ceiling electrical boxes need protection from overspray

Lightweight plastic pin-up over window and door openings to catch overspray fallout from ceiling work. Not intricate masking — quick pin-up that protects openings whether or not they will later be painted. Covers both windows and doors.

adjacent_surfaces.spec_impact: NO edge tasks — wall painter establishes ceiling line. Declaration exists for project-level finish group optimization only.

conditions_identified.effect: Height modifier applies. Scaffold/lift setup adds fixed time.
conditions_identified.notes: Ceilings above 14ft require scaffold or lift, significantly impacting all overhead tasks

conditions_identified.effect: Occupied spaces may restrict spray methods due to overspray and fumes. May force roll-only.
conditions_identified.notes: NC is typically unoccupied, but phased occupancy can occur in multi-unit projects

conditions_identified.effect: Poor ventilation restricts spray methods and slows all work.
conditions_identified.notes: Enclosed spaces without HVAC running require additional ventilation setup

inherited_research_corrections.title: Do not specify dry times in specs
inherited_research_corrections.impact: No dry time references in any artifact

notes_for_sop_librarian: Ceiling-only scope — no wall tasks, no edge work
Assumes ceilings already primed (not in this spec's scope)
Single coat for QT2-QT3; Two coats for QT4-QT5
QT4+ includes light sand between coats
Overhead work is slower than wall work — factor into task descriptions
Protection tasks must include protection_metadata per completeness doctrine
Site condition rules must be declared on affected tasks
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Ceiling SF is the only surface quantity driver
Overhead work factor: ~15-20% slower than equivalent wall rates
No edge work labor — ceiling painter can roll into wall area
QT4 adds light sand between coats + second finish coat
Fixture protection uses room count heuristic (6 lights + 2 ceiling boxes per room avg)
Height modifiers from Modifier_Registry.md (H1-H4) apply — more aggressive for overhead
Sheen application penalty: eggshell 1.18x, satin 1.18x, semi-gloss 1.43x, gloss 1.43x per production.json pattern
Spray+backroll coupling: backroll rate is the bottleneck
assumptions: Ceilings are already primed (separate prime spec)
Standard ceiling heights 8-10 ft (adjust rates for higher ceilings)
Subfloor only — no finished flooring installed (typical NC pre-trim)
Walls will be painted AFTER ceilings (wall painter establishes ceiling line)
Flat white or similar ceiling color (single color throughout) is the typical case

qt2_scope_analysis.summary: QT2 for NC ceiling finish is economy-grade work with minimal prep and single coat flat application. Inspection and repair are SKIPPED entirely (economy work does not include post-prime inspection). Single coat flat ceiling paint applied via any method. Application quality is NOT reduced — drips, sags, and holidays still fail at QT2. Final inspection is quick visual only.
included_tasks: TSK_PROTECT_CEILING_FIXTURES (binary - same at all tiers, spray methods only)
TSK_VERIFY_MASK_OPENINGS (binary - same at all tiers, spray methods only)
TSK_ROLL_CEILING_FINISH_R1 / TSK_SPRAY_CEILING_FINISH_R1 / TSK_BACKROLL_CEILING_FINISH_R1 / TSK_SPRAY_CEILING_FINISH_ONLY (binary - same at all tiers)
excluded_tasks: TSK_INSPECT_PRIMED_CEILING (QT3+ only - no inspection at QT2)
TSK_SPACKLE_CEILING_DEFECTS (QT3+ only - no repair at QT2)

reduced_tasks.qt2_behavior: Quick visual scan for major misses only. No detailed inspection.
reduced_tasks.qt2_rate: 2000 SF/hr (same as QT3 for final inspection)

inspection_standard.notes: QT2 skips pre-application inspection entirely. Final inspection is quick visual only for major misses (holidays, drips).

acceptable: Minor lap marks (flat ceiling paint is forgiving)
Texture variations visible only at close inspection
unacceptable: Major lap marks visible at distance

disclaimers: QT2 is for economy/rental grade work only
Single coat flat ONLY - no eggshell, satin, or semi-gloss at QT2
No inspection or repair - customer accepts minor imperfections from prime phase
Application quality is NOT reduced at QT2 - only prep intensity
Drips, sags, and holidays fail at ALL quality tiers including QT2
qt2_scope_analysis.nc_specific_notes: QT2 ceiling finish relies on proper priming from SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_NC_PRIME. Since inspection/repair is skipped at QT2, any defects in the primer coat will telegraph through the finish. This is the economy trade-off.
